systemic_cause.summary: Each slow test pays a fixed cost of about 17 s per process the first time the tcl_spectcl bundled pack set loads. run_pipeline (lib.rs:213-224) calls registry_for_dialect = tcl_spectcl::bundled::active_registry_for_dialect (bundled.rs:471). That calls registry_for_dialect -> registry_with_packs(profile, packs()) (bundled.rs:495-504). packs() (bundled.rs:404-411) is a per-process OnceLock that loads and evaluates all 8 EDA .tclspec packs (35,136 lines, 2.0 MB; eda_xilinx is 20,902 lines) from specs/ (discovery.rs:306-311, debug only) in an opt-level-0 build. nextest runs each test in its own process (CI ci.yml:1415, make test-rust, and the sol-26 harness), so the OnceLock never amortises and all 105 tests pay it.
evidence: tests::supplied_analysis_input_controls_the_document_pipeline runs the same run_pipeline_with_inputs (declared surface, interprocedural, memory SSA, deep semantic) on "set value 1" but with an ingress registry, not packs: 0.29-0.31 s for the whole process.

retained_explorer_source_tests::fixture() builds the unit with the pack-free default_context_registry: retained_explorer_source_keeps_actual_profiles... builds 6 dialect pipelines in 1.94-2.0 s, and the other fixture tests take 0.34-0.56 s.
bounds_withdraws_if_a_function_loses_its_actual_module_metadata = fixture() (cheap) plus one crate::run_pipeline call: 18.2 s.

original_document_pipeline_keeps_root_and_later_bom_roles calls run_pipeline for 9 dialects (9 registry overlays) in 17.6 s, about the same as single-call tests (16.9-18). So the per-profile overlay (tcl-registry cache.rs:244-271) is cheap and the once-per-process packs() load dominates.
Tests that never call run_pipeline (meta, segments, cst, formatters, view_tree unavailable-* tests) take 0.01-0.02 s, so harness and process start-up cost is negligible.

Regression lead: frozen091/explorer-event091 (docs/design/analysis/name-resolution-proofs/rust-validation/frozen091/explorer-event091/tests.log:69) ran original_event_semantic_view_preserves_conditional_descriptor_without_worker_grant, which calls run_pipeline twice, in 2.21 s in its own debug process. Today that test takes 17.4-17.7 s.

proposals.change: Factor run_pipeline into run_pipeline_with_registry(source, dialect, registry). run_pipeline then just passes &registry_for_dialect(dialect). Add a #[cfg(test)] pub(crate) fn run_pipeline_core(source, dialect) that passes tcl_registry::model::ingress::static_context_for_profile(profile).commands(), which is exactly what tcl_spectcl::install::registry_with_packs returns for an empty pack set (install.rs:76-79). In the test modules (serialise.rs, render.rs, view_tree.rs, wasm_explorer.rs, asm.rs and the lib.rs tests not listed under P2), change `use crate::run_pipeline` to `use crate::run_pipeline_core as run_pipeline`. Assertion text, inputs and dialects stay the same. Every test input is a non-EDA dialect (tcl8.6 x54, f5-irules x8, tcl9.0/9.1 x3 each, jim, tk, unknown), and every EDA pack command is behind required_package. wasm_explorer::tests::wasm_entries already compiles WASM against static_context_for(...).commands(), so this also makes the unit and codegen use the same registry.

proposals.class: KEEP on the real entry point (deep tier)
proposals.change: Keep 3 tests on the real run_pipeline/pack path so the shipped entry-point wiring stays covered: tests::run_pipeline_top_level_only, tests::unparseable_dialect_does_not_panic and tests::original_document_pipeline_keeps_root_and_later_bom_roles (the 9-dialect sweep). Optional, with sign-off: put them in `mod bundled_pack_path` so a local light run can exclude them with a nextest filter.

Measure tcl_spectcl::bundled::packs() alone in a debug binary and split the time into read/disk cache, evaluate_pack_cached and merge. Then choose between: (a) [profile.dev.package.<hot crate>] opt-level, following the precedent at Cargo.toml:233-242; (b) a lazy per-pack or per-profile load, so a non-EDA dialect does not evaluate 35k lines of vendor specs (this needs a product owner decision because the bundled tier deliberately carries all 8 packs for every dialect); (c) bisect against frozen091 (2.2 s) to see whether this is a regression. This also speeds up tcl explore, tcl-cli explorer_gui and tcl-mcp in debug.

Add a .config/nextest.toml override: [[profile.default.overrides]] filter = "package(tcl-explorer)", slow-timeout = { period = "20s", terminate-after = 3 }. This uses the existing mechanism; a test that becomes slower than today's pack-path cost is then marked SLOW in CI and killed at 60 s, with no wall-clock assertions in the tests.

tcl-explorer has no smoke test today. Add one smoke_ test that uses run_pipeline_core on a small proc + if script and checks that serialise_result has non-null ir, cfgPreSsa, sccp and stats with a ::p procedure row. Add its row to scripts/dev/smoke-targets.tsv (the cargo xtask smoke-targets check drift gate requires it). It runs under make smoke / make smoke-p P=tcl-explorer.

tiers.smoke: P5 smoke_ test (<1 s), selected by the nextest smoke profile filter test(/(::|^)smoke/) and smoke-targets.tsv.
tiers.deep: All 140 tcl_explorer lib tests, unchanged in number: rust-tests-shard 3 (scripts/dev/rust-test-binary-shards.tsv:142) and make test-rust / make test before a PR. 137 run sub-second to about 3 s on run_pipeline_core; the 3 P2 tests stay on the real pack path (about 17 s each until P3).
tiers.exhaustive: none. Do not #[ignore] the pack-path tests: the exhaustive tier never runs before a PR.
tiers.local_light_iteration: `cargo nextest run -p tcl-explorer -E "package(tcl-explorer) - test(/bundled_pack_path/)"` after P2, or plain `cargo test -p tcl-explorer --lib`, which uses a single process, so packs() loads once (about 17 s plus the remainder) even today.

buckets.F2: Definitions not lowered: proc / oo::class method / iRules when bodies are lowered as plain IRCall (e.g. "call proc p  return FIRST"), so procedure/method/handler rows are missing. Also seen on the fast fixture-built path (retained_event_order_* returns 0 rows), so the cause is in tcl-compiler lowering rather than in run_pipeline alone.
buckets.F1/F2: Symptom fits both F1 and F2; which one fails first depends on the input.
buckets.F3: A supplied ResolvedAnalysisInput is still not kept on the module (lib.rs:320: source_metadata_input is None). This is the run_pipeline_with_analysis_input path that the LSP uses, so it is a likely product bug and probably the same root as F1.
buckets.F4: Inventory or contract drift that does not depend on the pipeline: ARTIFACT_COVERAGE lacks CompilationUnit::source_class_facts and related fields (luna-25 already flagged this), and remaining_actual_cu_views expects every view to be an array while taintReplays is now an object {scope,status,complete,...}.
